title: Support Vector Machine
description: Margin-maximizing classifier using kernel functions for non-linear boundaries.
name: Support Vector Machine
summary: Support Vector Machines find the hyperplane that maximizes the margin between different classes. Using the kernel trick, they map low-dimensional inputs into high-dimensional space to solve complex non-linear classifications.
use_when: Working with high-dimensional datasets containing moderate sample sizes, such as text classification or genomics.
avoid_when: Dataset size exceeds tens of thousands of samples, as training complexity scales quadratically.
pros: Effective in high-dimensional spaces, even when feature count exceeds sample count.
Memory efficient because it only uses a subset of training points (support vectors).
Highly versatile due to support for custom and standard kernel functions (RBF, linear, poly).
cons: Quadratic training time complexity O(N^2) makes it scale poorly to large datasets.
Does not directly provide probability estimates; requires computationally expensive calibration.
Highly sensitive to noise and outliers near the margin.

key_hyperparams.name: kernel
key_hyperparams.note: Specifies the kernel type to be used in the algorithm. Standard choices are 'linear', 'poly', 'rbf'.

quick_start:
from sklearn.svm import SVC
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[-1, -1], [-2, -1], [1, 1], [2, 1]])
y = np.array([1, 1, 2, 2])
clf = SVC(kernel='rbf').fit(X, y)
preds = clf.predict([[0.8, 1]])
